title: Career roadmap · Carbon Analyst
summary: A Carbon Analyst measures greenhouse-gas emissions, supports carbon accounting and reporting, and helps organisations identify opportunities to reduce emissions and meet climate targets.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a 3-year B.Sc route, with an optional 4-year honours/research year. If the degree follows a 4-year structure, use the additional year for advanced carbon accounting, research, internships and a substantial climate-data project.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build climate science, GHG accounting, Excel/SQL, carbon-footprinting and reporting skills; target Carbon Analyst, Sustainability Analyst or ESG Analyst entry roles.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Specialise in corporate carbon accounting, Scope 1–3 emissions, GHG Protocol reporting, LCA, ESG disclosures or carbon markets.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Move toward Carbon Consultant, Climate Data Specialist, Sustainability Manager, Carbon Accounting Lead or Climate Risk roles.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine climate science with automation, climate data, AI-assisted emissions analysis, transition planning and emerging carbon-management standards.

blocks.text: PhD routes
Potential research directions include:

The strongest long-term profile will combine climate-domain expertise + carbon accounting + data analytics + technology + policy understanding. Senior professionals should be able to interpret emissions inventories, challenge data quality, evaluate decarbonisation strategies, communicate with business leaders and use increasingly automated climate-data systems.
